title: Validate evaluation metrics before using them to select agent behavior
applies_when: Adopting a third-party deterministic score as a judge, reward, routing signal or research outcome, especially unordered tool-call matching and rank correlation with tied or constant inputs.
lesson: Validate the score against its mathematical contract, not merely that it executes and stays in [0,1]. For an explicitly order-insensitive matcher, permute the same calls and use a small exhaustive assignment oracle to check exact versus partial credits. Future AGI's pinned tool_call_accuracy YAML greedily consumes an expected slot: [search(wrong), search(right)] against [search(right)] scores 0.25, while reversing the same actual multiset scores 0.5. For Spearman, compare tied ranks against an independent implementation; the no-ties squared-rank-distance shortcut does not apply to midranks. Test constant inputs separately and preserve undefinedness rather than interpreting an apparent perfect score as evidence. Test the exact deployed representation: Python, YAML templates and persisted database copies may differ.
avoid_when: Order invariance is inappropriate for a metric whose contract intentionally grades action sequence. Maximum-credit assignment is a small-domain diagnostic, not automatically the intended metric or a scalable implementation. A product may define an explicit fallback for undefined correlation; do not invent that policy. Executing complete YAML bodies validates only that boundary, not sandbox dispatch, seeding, API behavior or the full platform. These known public defects are development controls, not fresh discoveries or proof that a particular agent-selection policy improves PR yield, recall or cost. Check existing issue/PR ownership before proposing a repair.

evidence.note: Exact platform template defines full/name-only credits and greedily marks slots used. This supports the retry/reordering counterexample, not deployed API or database validation.
Exact template assigns average ranks but uses the no-ties d-squared shortcut, with no zero-variance guard. Source evidence for the specific calculation, not a universal platform verdict.
Independent definition/reference API; constant inputs produce ConstantInputWarning and NaN because correlation is undefined. It does not choose a product's normalized fallback policy.
Existing public report includes the greedy tool-matching and Spearman defects. This establishes prior reporting; do not treat reproduction as a novel competing PR.
